# STM32H743 AIO Nano Flight Controller + 4-in-1 ESC (Job #67): Architecture, Loss Model, DShot DMA Plan, Netlist

## 0. Architecture Clarification and Headline Finding

**Architecture.** The STM32H743 runs ArduPilot and generates bidirectional DShot600. It does **not** commutate the motors. The 48 kHz PWM is generated by per-channel ESC MCUs running AM32 or BLHeli_32, for example an AT32F421 or STM32G071 per motor. ArduPilot cannot run ESC firmware, so the design is split into:

- **FC domain:** H743, IMU, baro, OSD, DShot output, eRPM capture.
- **ESC domain:** 4× (ESC MCU + 3-phase gate driver + 6 MOSFETs + current sense).

**Headline finding.** An 80 A per-channel burst is not thermally achievable on a 20×20 mm "nano" board. The model in Section 3 shows:

- 4 × 80 A burst produces about 90 W of loss into roughly 4 J/K of board heat capacity.
- That is a temperature rise of more than 20 K/s, so the board exceeds silicon limits in about 3–4 s even before MOSFET junction transients are considered.
- The physically defensible ratings are about **50 A for 5 s burst and about 18–25 A continuous per channel**, depending on airflow.

Recommendation: either derate the product to those figures, or move to a 30.5×30.5 board with 5×6 mm DFN MOSFETs if 80 A is a hard requirement.

All component parameters below are **assumed example values**. Replace them with datasheet values for the selected parts before sign-off.

| MOSFET R_DS(on) @ 25 °C, V_GS = 10 V | R_25 | 1.0 mΩ (40 V, 3.3×3.3 DFN class) |

| Output charge | Q_oss | 40 nC |

## 2. Loss Model (per motor channel)

### 2.1 Conduction Loss

In 120° six-step commutation with synchronous rectification, current always flows through two legs:

- The **PWM leg**: the high-side FET for D, then the low-side FET for 1−D.
- The **return leg**: the low-side FET, on 100% of the time.

The duty cycle therefore cancels:

$$P_{cond} = 2\,R_{DS,hot}\,I_{rms}^2,\qquad I_{rms}^2 = I^2 + \frac{\Delta I^2}{12}$$

$$I_{rms}^2 = 6400 + 8.3 = 6408\ \text{A}^2$$

$$P_{cond} = 2(1.5\times10^{-3})(6408) = \mathbf{19.2\ W}$$

Electro-thermal coupling should be solved iteratively, because R_DS(on) depends on Tj:

$$R(T_j) = R_{25}\,[1+\alpha(T_j-25)],\quad \alpha\approx0.006/\text{K}$$

### 2.2 Switching Loss (hard-switched edges on the PWM leg)

$$P_{sw} = \tfrac12 V_{bus} I (t_r+t_f) f_{sw} = 0.5(25.2)(80)(30\text{n})(48\text{k}) = \mathbf{1.45\ W}$$

### 2.3 Dead-Time Body-Diode Conduction (two edges per period)

$$P_{dt} = 2 V_F I\, t_{dt} f_{sw} = 2(0.8)(80)(200\text{n})(48\text{k}) = \mathbf{1.23\ W}$$

This term scales with dead time. The ESC firmware dead-time setting is a direct thermal lever: 100 ns gives 0.61 W.

### 2.4 Reverse Recovery, C_oss, and Gate Drive

$$P_{rr} = Q_{rr} V_{bus} f_{sw} = 50\text{n}(25.2)(48\text{k}) = 0.06\ \text{W}$$

$$P_{oss} = \tfrac12 Q_{oss} V_{bus} f_{sw} = 0.024\ \text{W}$$

$$P_{gate} = Q_g V_{GS} f_{sw} \times 2 = 0.058\ \text{W}$$

The gate-drive term is dissipated mostly in the driver and gate resistors, not the FETs.
